pahārāda.notes: AN 8.19 is the conversation with Pahārāda, lord of the asuras, about the ocean. The hit at the end of AN 8.20 is the chapter recap.

pahāsa.notes: SN 42.2:2.11 explicitly calls the hell pahāso nāma nirayo. Sujato translates its name as ‘Laughter’, so the packet misses it. The references place the citation in SN 42.1, one discourse early.

pajjota.notes: MN 108:2.1 names King Pajjota as the reason Ajātasattu is fortifying Rājagaha. The candidate describes a tank built by Duṭṭhagāmaṇī near Kāsapabbata. MN 51 gives no evidence for that tank.

pajjunna.notes: DPPN explicitly includes the thundering deity of DN 20, Kokanadā’s father, and the name in the invocation at DN 32:10.17 in this entry. The two daughters appear in SN 1.39 and 1.40. SN 1.38 is the adjacent splinter discourse.

palāsavana.notes: MN 68 and AN 10.67–68 place the grove at Naḷakapāna. The citations also land in MN 67 at Cātumā and AN 10.66 at Nālaka in Magadha.

panāda.notes: DN 20:10.7 and DN 32:10.6 both list Panāda with Opamañña. Thag 2.22:1.1 explicitly calls its Panāda a king. The packet has no entry for that king.

pasenadi.notes: AN 5.49 names Pasenadi at Mallikā’s death. AN 5.50 is about Muṇḍa and Bhaddā. AN 5.31 names Princess Sumanā without naming Pasenadi, and AN 5.30 and SN 6.10–12 give no mention of the king. DPPN cites Ud 6.2 for his respect for other sects, but at 8.1 Pasenadi reveals that the men he saluted were his own spies.

pañcakaṅga.notes: The discussion with Udāyī is in MN 59 and SN 36.19, and the gathering at Pañcakaṅga’s house is in MN 127. MN 58, SN 36.18 and MN 126 are adjacent page hits. SN 36.20 mentions him only in the recap.

pañcasikha.notes: DPPN’s DN i.220 maps to DN 11, but Pañcasikha’s report is in DN 19. DN 21:1.6.5 dates his song to when the Buddha was newly awakened. DPPN dates it before the awakening. The unlisted occurrence at SN 35.123:2.3 is a chapter recap of his question in SN 35.119.

pañcasālā.notes: SN 4.18 opens in the Magadhan brahmin village. The adjacent SN 4.17 opens at Vesālī.

pañcālacaṇḍa.notes: SN 2.7 calls the speaker a devaputta. AN 9.42 quotes his verse and gives him the same title. DN 32:10.16 gives only the name in a list of yakkhas. DPPN itself calls their identity probable, so the yakkha sense remains open. SN 2.5, 2.6 and 2.8 name other speakers. SN 2.10 has the name in a chapter recap.

paṇḍara.notes: Thag 17.1:1.3 identifies Phussa’s questioner by his clan in paṇḍarasagotto, and 3.2 addresses him as isipaṇḍarasavhaya. Both compounds have their own dictionary lines. The DPD sense here describes a type of elephant.

paṇḍava.notes: The entry cites two Theragāthā verses, but the references place only Thag 1.41. Thag 20.1:28.2 also names Paṇḍava alongside Vebhāra.

paṇḍitakumāraka.notes: AN 3.74:1.2 names both Licchavis visiting Ānanda. AN 3.73 is the visit of Mahānāma the Sakyan, and DPD’s AN 3.75 is one discourse later in this edition.

paṭācārā.notes: AN 1.238 names the nun foremost in Vinaya. The two flanking AN groups are page overlaps. Her own poem, Thig 5.10, describes washing her feet and drawing out the lamp wick. The passage on losing her husband, children, parents and brother appears in Thig 10.1, attributed to Kisāgotamī. Thig 7.1:4.2 also refers to Paṭācārā’s teaching in the compound paṭācārānusāsaniṁ.

phagguna.notes: DPD specifies Moḷiyaphagguna, called by that full name at MN 21:2.1 and SN 12.12:2.1. The packet misses the vocative phagguna at SN 12.12:7.1. DPPN describes the questioner of SN 35.83 and tentatively links him to the sick monk of AN 6.56. Neither discourse gives the epithet or links him to MN 21. AN 6.56:8.2–3 attributes release from the five lower fetters to him. DPPN’s claim of arahantship goes further. AN 6.55 and SN 35.81–82 are adjacent citations.

phalagaṇḍa.notes: SN 1.50:3.1 and SN 2.24:4.1 both list him between Upaka and Pukkusāti among the seven freed monks in Aviha. Both read palagaṇḍo, which taps through to DPD’s separate palagaṇḍa 2. SN 1.49 is a page overlap.

pilakkhaguhā.notes: MN 76:2.1 places Sandaka in the cave. The page also maps to MN 75.

pilindavaccha.notes: AN 1.215 names the monk dear to the deities. The adjacent AN groups are page overlaps. Ud 3.6:4.4 explains his habitual form of address by five hundred successive brahmin births. The entry gives one hundred. Thag 1.9 attributes the verse to him, and Thag 1.10 names him in the recap.

pilotika.notes: The exchange between Jāṇussoṇi and the wanderer is in MN 27. The page also maps to MN 26.

piyadassī.notes: MN 116:4.6 explicitly calls this Piyadassī a paccekasambuddha of Mount Isigili. The DPD sense for the previous Buddha cites the Buddhavaṁsa.

piyaka.notes: AN 5.50:1.5 names Piyaka as Muṇḍa’s treasurer. The adjacent AN 5.49 concerns Pasenadi’s grief for Mallikā.

piṅgalakoccha.notes: MN 30:2.1 names the brahmin in both languages, piṅgalakoccho in Pāli and Piṅgalakoccha in English. Joining DPPN’s ‘Piṅgala Koccha’ preserves the capital K, so the packet’s case-sensitive filter misses him.

piṅgiya.notes: Snp 5.1 and 5.18 list Piṅgiya among the sixteen brahmin students. He asks about old age in 5.17 and recites the Way to the Far Shore in 5.19. SN 1.50:3.4 and SN 2.24:4.4 give the Aviha monk’s name as siṅgiyo and saṅgiyo respectively. Sujato uses Piṅgiya for both, but neither sutta is in the packet’s allowed list. SN 1.49 is a page overlap. The texts do not establish DPPN’s proposed link between the two biographies.

piṅgiyānī.notes: AN 5.194:1.3 calls him a brahmin and AN 5.195 tells of his verse before the Licchavis. The packet supplies only the Jātaka queen’s sense. The tapped forms also have DPD’s masculine lemma piṅgiyāni, with short final i, which would fit this entry. AN 5.193 is about Saṅgārava. AN 5.200:7.2 repeats the name in a chapter recap.

piṇḍola.notes: MN 116:4.8 explicitly calls Piṇḍola a paccekasambuddha. The monk in DPD’s SN 35.127 example appears under his full name piṇḍolabhāradvājo and has a separate candidate under that lemma. The short form piṇḍolo also occurs in the chapter recaps at Thag 2.10:3.1, SN 48.50:12.4 and Ud 4.10:5.3.

piṇḍolabhāradvāja.notes: AN 1.195 names the disciple foremost in the lion’s roar. King Udena questions him in SN 35.127. The two flanking AN groups and SN 35.125–126 are page overlaps. DPPN reverses the speaker in Ud 4.6:3.1, where the Buddha speaks after observing Piṇḍola meditating.

pokkharaṇiyā.notes: AN 6.21:1.1 supplies the location at Sāmagāmaka. Sujato renders pokkharaṇiyāyaṁ as ‘by a lotus pond’. DPPN attributes its identification as a monastery to the commentary.

posāla.notes: Snp 5.1 lists Posāla among Bāvarī’s pupils. The cited question and answer are in Snp 5.15, which the verse references failed to place.
